title: Smart Boards vs. Blackboards: ‘Kabir Sir Ka Akhri Lesson’ Strikes an Emotional Chord at IFFI
subtitle: Filmmaker reflects on the changing relationship between teachers and students in the age of technology
body_text:
Posted On: 27 NOV 2026 3:17PM by PIB Mumbai Release ID: 2342508 Views: 84 A A Print Share X Facebook Instagram WhatsApp Copy Article Link
Read in: English Urdu Kannada
Goa, 27 November 2026 What happens when teachers who once shaped generations find themselves struggling to keep pace with changing classrooms? This question lies at the heart of Kabir Sir Ka Akhri Lesson , the debut Hindi feature film by filmmaker Sarfaraz Alam, which had its World Premiere at the 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI). The film draws inspiration from an experience that Alam encountered during a visit to his childhood school in Bihar's Nalanda district. He found that traditional blackboards had given way to smart boards, while veteran teachers were struggling to adapt to the new technologies. What he witnessed prompted him to reflect on the changing realities of the teaching profession and the challenges faced by educators today. Recalling the experience during a press conference organised by the Press Information Bureau (PIB) in Goa today, Alam said, “Two years ago, when I visited my school, I saw my teachers struggling with new technologies as smart boards replaced the blackboard. That is how the idea came in.” Tracing his journey from a modest village school in Bihar to studying medicine in Russia and subsequently pursuing filmmaking at the New York Film Academy, Alam spoke about the lasting influence of his teachers and the connection he continues to share with his roots. He observed that educators who once guided generations of doctors, engineers and IAS officers are today navigating technological barriers and changing attitudes towards the teaching profession. “This movie is based on what they are facing today and how they are treated. It will connect with audiences across the entire country,” he said. Produced by Kartina Entertainment and Sports Private Limited, the 103.52-minute Hindi drama features acclaimed actor Vinay Pathak in the lead role. Alam praised Pathak's performance and also reflected on the changing dynamics between teachers, students and parents. He noted that the close emotional bond that once characterised teacher-student relationships is increasingly missing from modern education. Emphasising the importance of thoughtful communication, he urged young people to observe and listen carefully rather than speak ill of others. Speaking about Bihar, Alam highlighted the state's infrastructural progress and underscored the role of cinema in bringing its development and achievements to wider audiences. Beyond the transition from blackboards to smart boards, Kabir Sir Ka Akhri Lesson raises questions about respect, changing generations and the place of teachers in an evolving society. Its story, rooted in a filmmaker's personal experience, touches upon a universal relationship that transcends geographical and cultural boundaries. This resonates with the theme of the 57th IFFI, being held in Goa from November 20 to 28, 2026: ‘Stories Without Borders’. The press conference was moderated by Shri Vivek Vishwas.
